value: males chose the red colour labelled 650 nm (RGB LED panel at R 255, G 0, B 0) most often, significantly more than the other five colours; selection of the colours labelled 520 nm, 580 nm and the white control (CK) did not differ significantly
method: behavioural: choice among six colours shown on 10 W RGB LED panels, one per arena room of a darkroom hexagonal maze, males; colours named by wavelength through Bruton's wavelength-to-RGB conversion (labels 380, 440, 520, 580, 650 nm, white CK); emission spectra not measured
conditions: Beetles tested in a darkroom in a black-cardboard hexagonal maze (base edge 20 cm); a light was scored as preferred if the adult stayed in its arena room more than 1 min; 100 males and 100 females tested separately, 10 beetles per run, 3 replicates. No emission spectrum was measured (illuminance only, Sigma AS803), so the labels are nominal: the '380 nm' stimulus is a red-plus-blue mix with no UV emission shown, and '650 nm' is the panel's red primary at full level. Percentages appear only in Figure 3. The wavelength-preference test shows what beetles chose, and, with unmeasured broad-band panel colours of unequal brightness, does not separate colour choice from attraction to brightness, nor test response to any single wavelength. The omitted middle of the sentence gives the test statistic, F5,12 = 19.96, p < 0.001, and the lowest male rates as 380 nm and 440 nm. Beetles were newly emerged adults bought from Shijialing Biodiverse Farm, Shandong, fed grapes and peaches between tests; how often each beetle was reused is not stated.

quote: Statistically, for females of S. frugiperda, there were no significant differences between the three light sources (F2,20 = 2.723, p = 0.09).
note: Same paper and licence notes as the male record. Sentence seen verbatim on two fetches of the mdpi.com page (fragments joined).

value: green LED trap (peak about 521-524 nm) had the highest recapture among six LED colours: 67% of the wasps recaptured (percentage recapture = count on a trap divided by the total recaptured, Section 2.5), significantly higher than all other colours (p = 0.0001)
method: behavioural: 24 h multiple-choice cage assay, parasitoids released and recaptured on sticky traps carrying UV, blue, cyan, green, yellow and red LEDs
conditions: Climate chamber 25 +/- 1 C, 18 h light:6 h dark; 40 wasps released per run from 0.7 m; two cages (0.8 x 1 x 1 m) used at once; 20 replicates with the cage as unit. LED colour had a significant effect on mean recapture (F = 94.7, df = 5, p = 0.001); 61% of all released wasps were recaptured on the six traps. Every LED trap except UV was adjusted to equal photon flux, 8.1 umol m-2 s-1; UV was measured with a UV-A sensor and converted to photon flux density but not adjusted, and the paper gives no reason (tool reading). Recapture on a sticky trap records arrival and landing, so it combines colour choice with attraction to light; the parasitoid's spectral sensitivity was not measured. Of all wasps released, 61% were recaptured on the six traps, so the green trap held about 41% of those released. In the greenhouse, E. formosa preferred the standard yellow sticky trap over the green-LED-enhanced yellow trap (94% against 6% of recaptured wasps, p = 0.016, choice test), and only 9% were recaptured on the LED-enhanced trap in no-choice tests with or without hosts (Abstract, Results), so the laboratory green preference did not make the LED trap attractive in the greenhouse. A modified green trap with a white background drew 61% at 18.03 umol m-2 s-1 and 4% at 25.60 umol m-2 s-1 (Results 3.3), so the green response depends on intensity; the colour test was run at 8.1. Wasps were about 24 h old and unmated, sex not stated, from Katz Biotech AG.
